newsitem.title: ITALY: Five ex-bankers arrested in Italian probe.
newsitem.headline: Five ex-bankers arrested in Italian probe.

text.p: The ex-chairman of the southern Italian development bank Isveimer and four former executives were arrested on Tuesday on suspicion of false accounting, judicial sources said.

The five were arrested on a warrant issued by a Naples magistrate who is investigating suspected bookkeeping irregularities at the institution, which was majority owned by Banco Di Napoli until it was put into liquidation earlier this year.
Police searched the headquarters of the bank as part of the investigation.
Banco di Napoli held 64.8 percent of Isveimer and the Italian Treasury held 33 percent.
Among those arrested was Giuseppe Di Vagno, who was chairman of the institution for 10 years until 1993. Isveimer specialised in loans to help Italian industry in the poorer south.

Before Isveimer was liquidated, Banco di Napoli recorded a 3.16 trillion lire loss ($2.02 billion) for 1995, almost treble its 1994 losses. The Treasury has put 60 percent of Banco di Napoli up for sale.
